name: Demo: technology adoption in small firms (synthetic)
case_description: The cases are 60 owner-managed firms with 10 to 49 employees, in light manufacturing and wholesale distribution. Over an 18-month period the same software vendor offered each of them a cloud-based inventory and order-management system. Adoption was a voluntary decision taken by the owner-manager, usually after a trial period, and it carried real costs: staff had to be retrained, spreadsheets and paper routines were retired, and the firm became dependent on the vendor for updates and support. Firms differed in how far the owner-manager trusted the vendor, in how strongly the firm's management team backed a change, and in how much slack the firm had in budget and staff time. At the end of the period, adoption was observed as the extent to which the system was actually used in daily operations, from a nominal login that changed nothing, through partial use for some tasks, to full reliance for ordering, invoicing and stock control. The study asks which firms ended up using the system extensively.

variables.name: TRUST
variables.construct_definition: Managerial trust in the technology vendor.
variables.instrument: Mean of four 7-point Likert items (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree).

variables.name: SUPPORT
variables.construct_definition: Perceived top-management support for the system.
variables.instrument: Mean of three 7-point Likert items (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree).

variables.name: RESOURCES
variables.instrument: Composite index of budget, staff time and training capacity, scaled 0-100.

variables.name: ADOPTION
variables.construct_definition: Extent to which the system is used in daily operations.
